svg.title: Four stages from shallow redirect to invariant-preserving memo merge
svg.desc: Stage 1 redirects a group but leaves stale child IDs. Stage 2 rewrites child IDs but can create duplicate expression keys. Stage 3 processes collision-driven group merges to a fixed point. Stage 4 uses parent backlinks to target each individual rewrite while also preserving stale handles and winners.
svg.text: Each local repair exposes the next global invariant
Redirect the losing group
move_group(merge_into, merge_from)
Failure symptom: stored expressions still contain the old child ID.
A later insertion misses deduplication and creates a duplicate group.
Missing invariant: every stored child is its canonical group.
Rewrite affected child IDs
canonicalize_expr(old_expr)
Failure symptom: two old keys become the same new key.
Their owner groups remain separate unless the collision is merged.
Missing invariant: equal expression keys imply equivalent owners.
Process collisions to a fixed point
while let Some(pair) = worklist.pop()
Repair: canonicalize each pair, rewrite parents, and push newly
discovered owner-group collisions until no work remains.
Boundary: scanning the whole memo finds parents but repeats work.
Follow parent backlinks
parent_exprs[merge_from]
Repair: target expressions whose keys can change, then maintain
the reverse index through every rewrite and collision.
Cross-cutting state: redirects, stale handles, and cheaper winners.
Done only when every materialized view of equivalence agrees
